chunks: And through his chain of narration, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from 'Amir ibn 'Abdillah, who said:

I said to Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I paid two or three gold coins extra to my cameldriver to take me through Madinah.' He said, 'You have done well! How easy this is for you: you come to the grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). Indeed, he hears you from nearby, and it is conveyed to him; it is conveyed to him from you from afar.'

key_terms.قَبْرَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The grave of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: Does the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) hear those who visit his grave?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the spiritual merit of visiting the Prophet’s grave, emphasizing the concept of *Istiqra’* (the Prophet’s awareness of visitors). The narration highlights the metaphysical connection between the living and the deceased, affirming that the Prophet not only hears the greetings but that the message is conveyed to him from a distance, a key tenet in Shia jurisprudence regarding *Salat al-Ghabt* and *Tashih al-Ziyarah*.
